items.title: Merge PR #57
items.body: Five changes and four checks, each with its A/B in bench/loop/. CI is green on the pushed head; the e2e suite passed locally (24 passed, 1 skipped by design). The Safari/iOS preload (R2) is kept as a fix, not on a measured win: the preload never ran there, and the bench could not call the gain. One trade-off to accept: on Safari's path (no idle callback) the creator's first frame was called 13% slower while the joiner's was faster in every pair. Both pages run on one VM in the bench, so the creator's frame competes with the joiner's piece builds.

rows.only: joiner’s first frame|creator’s first frame|long tasks total

items.recommend: Merge. R2's case is correctness (a preload that silently never ran on iOS). The creator's +13% is untested as a cause; I believe it is the two pages sharing one VM, since before this change iOS paid the same work inside the first board frame.

items.title: Four rows are slower than the first recorded run, none from this run; the worst bisected to #55
items.body: Against 92ce041 (2 pairs): create → share link shown +108%, the reopened game's main-thread script +38% (the warm-up the last run added, named there as its price), and the desktop start page +6–10%. Against main, the same rows are within noise (share link +4.8% over 4 pairs), so this branch did not cause them. Bisected the share link: only two commits lie between 92ce041 and main, and 150303c (#55, "a scene chunk that fails to load leaves the page's other parts up") moves it from 1.07 s to 1.92 s (+79%, both pairs; bisect-share-link-150303c-vs-92ce041.md). #55 changed how the lobby loads its scene and ends its moments (lazyChunk, ChunkBoundary, the noScene path in LobbyLayout.tsx); the share link waits on the lobby's choose beat. Not root-caused: the run's budget ended.

items.recommend: Treat it as a regression from #55 and root-cause it first in the next run (or ask its author): the creator now waits about 0.85 s longer for the link to share.

items.title: Should the client refuse illegal moves from the opponent?
items.body: The replay applies any move the server relays, and the server checks only turn order, so an opponent with devtools can move your pieces or jump across the board. README's "Scope and trust assumptions" calls that a non-goal ("the threat model is 'my friends'"), so I built the check, measured it and left it out. With a new allocation-free Board.isLegalMove, exhaustively cross-checked against the naive rules, a 3,000-ply replay was within noise (−3%). It adds +48 engine lines and an exhaustive test. The patch is in bench/loop/patches/replay-legality.patch.

charts.caption: Replay cost with the check, client tier.

items.recommend: Adopt it if the game will ever be shared beyond friends; it costs nothing a player would see. Otherwise leave it parked.

items.title: Seats can be taken with the link alone
items.body: A rejoin needs only the game id and a colour, so anyone with the invitation link can take a seat and evict its player (who then stops reconnecting). Related, from the same reviewer: gameId has no pattern, a socket has no rate limit, and a game has no ply cap. Each is a protocol change (server/schema.json).
items.recommend: Decide whether the threat model still holds. If not, a seat token issued at create/join is the first fix, with a migration window for stored seats.

items.title: CLAUDE.md lacks the sections this loop relies on
items.body: The perf-iteration prompt reads CLAUDE.md's North star, Measurement, Reporting, Loop state, Tests and session-log sections; none exists. I used "Performance" for measurement, bench/loop/ for the loop state and the e2e + vitest suites for tests, and kept the run record in bench/loop/RUN-20261001-0352.md.
items.recommend: Add a short "Loop state" section naming bench/loop/ (ledger, scoreboard.jsonl, tools, one RUN file per run) and a North star of a few lines, so the next run grades against your words, not mine.

items.body:

The piece set preloads on Safari and iOS too (637677f), kept as a fix
items.body: The idle preload returned early where requestIdleCallback is missing: every iOS browser and Safari without a flag (MDN browser-compat-data 8.1.3). There the whole set was built and baked inside the first frame that drew pieces. Now each piece is built and baked in its own task, on an idle callback or a 50 ms timer. preloadPieceSet is gone; the baked set's preload already did its work. The bench gained BENCH_NO_IDLE_CALLBACK=1 to time Safari's path.

items.title: Quiet marks shade fewer pixels (00db00a)
items.body: Every destination of a held piece drew on a quad sized for the soft pool that only a mark straight above or below the piece becomes: 1.03 units square instead of 0.70, about 2.1× the fragments, each running the marks' whole shader in software. The quad is now the ring's size unless the mark is soft. What it draws is unchanged.

charts.caption: Higher is better for fps rows. The orbit with nothing held draws no quiet mark, so its "worse" call is drift.

items.title: The game ships only its own piece set; one scheduler (d74b5c3, bb9840d)
items.body: The knight sculptor (knight.ts on sdf.ts and decimate.ts) shipped in the scene chunk though the game only draws the medium set, whose knight ships precomputed. pieceSet() is now that set alone, and pieces/sculpted.ts serves the gallery, benches and tests. The build also carried two extra copies of scheduler under r3f; resolve.dedupe leaves one. Geometry is byte-identical (golden hashes unchanged).

charts.caption: Bytes of the chunk the start page's preview and every game page load.

items.title: Rules that now run as checks (3c01202, 4a167f4, 7d59f20)
items.body:
• The build fails if three.js or r3f reaches the entry chunk; adding import { Vector3 } from 'three' to main.tsx fails it.
  • Two tests mount the real garden: its signature holds still at rest, and every garden material is one the signature can see into. A uniform nudged by 1e-9 a frame fails them.
  • e2e/programs.spec.ts: a whole game (a selection, a capture, check, mate) links no shader program after the warm-up. It counts linkProgram calls. It runs in full motion because under reduced motion its mutation passed.
  • The browser bench records each frame's garden mode (from the copy, taking it, or in full), and the loop's primary.mjs fails on a missing primary row instead of averaging fewer.

choices.intro:
• Pushed to the session's designated branch claude/optimistic-turing-ni8v5c; the prompt's improve/<run id> name is the local branch. The session forbids pushing elsewhere.
  • Kept R9 although one render row was called worse, because that row draws none of the changed code.
  • Kept R2 on correctness (the preload never ran on iOS), not on a called win; the creator's +13% on the Safari path is named as a trade-off with an untested cause.
  • Made the programs spec run in full motion (~50 s locally, its own 6-minute timeout), against CLAUDE.md's preference for reduced motion in tests that play on, because under reduced motion it could not fail.
  • Unit tests now hold the preload asleep (setupTests.ts), as jsdom's lack of an idle callback did before.
  • Installed Node 24.21.0 with nvm (the image ships 22; the repo pins 24) and pointed Playwright at the image's Chromium 141 headless shell.

notConfirmed.intro:
• The iPhone gain itself: Chromium without an idle callback stands in for Safari; no real iOS device was available.
  • Cloudflare Pages' cache headers (the reviewer's _headers idea): the preview host is blocked by this environment's network policy.
  • The startup tier (S1/S2) in the final A/B: the new startup bench called an API the base lacks, so only the head side ran. The bench now handles both shapes.
  • Pixel identity of R9: argued from the shader (nothing drawn beyond 1.11× the ring plus its stroke), not diffed.

merge.intro: No other sessions were active, so nothing to hand over.
